---
title: "camdl"
subtitle: "Compartmental Model Description Language"
toc: false
---

camdl is a language and toolkit for stochastic compartmental models of
epidemics. You write a `.camdl` file that says what the compartments are (for
example susceptible, infected and recovered), how individuals move between them
and how fast. The compiler checks the file and expands it into a flat model
description, which camdl then simulates and fits to data.

Most guides and reference pages here are the same text the binary carries:
`camdl docs <topic>` prints them offline, matched to the installed version.
The tutorials are website-only, because they show the real output of each
command, regenerated from the current code every time the site is built.

<!-- figure: architecture, caption: How camdl splits responsibility between the modeler and camdl's developers. The modeler states the model's structure and prior assumptions, and writes no simulation or inference code; camdl's job is to execute the declared model exactly. A trajectory that contradicts the declared model is therefore a bug in camdl, not in the modeler's work, and implementation risk moves from many privately maintained code bases to one shared, tested one. -->
